example_sentence: Researchers conducted a survey of two thousand university students.
collocations: conduct research; conduct a survey; conduct an experiment

notes: 學術寫作講「做研究」幾乎都用這個字，不用 do research

example_sentence: Migrant workers constitute nearly a third of the city's workforce.
collocations: constitute a threat; constitute a majority; constitute evidence
root_analysis: con-(一起) + stitut(建立, 同 institute/substitute) → 一起建立成 → 組成
synonyms: make up; form; comprise; account for

example_sentence: Many educators advocate replacing final exams with continuous assessment.
collocations: advocate a policy; advocate for reform; strongly advocate
root_analysis: ad-(朝向) + voc(聲音, 同 voice/vocal/vocation) + -ate → 為某事發聲
notes: Task 2 表達立場好用；名詞 an advocate of 也很常見

collocations: allocate resources; allocate funding; allocate time
root_analysis: ad-(朝向) + loc(地方, 同 location/local) + -ate → 放到該去的位置

example_sentence: The government implemented stricter penalties for repeat offenders.
collocations: implement a policy; implement measures; implement reforms
root_analysis: im-(進入) + ple(填滿, 同 complete/supplement) + -ment → 填滿內容 → 付諸實行
synonyms: carry out; enforce; put into practice; execute

example_sentence: Toxins from processed food gradually accumulate in the body.
collocations: accumulate wealth; accumulate evidence; accumulate over time
root_analysis: ac-(朝向) + cumul(堆積, 同 cumulative) + -ate → 一層層堆起來
synonyms: build up; amass; gather; pile up

example_sentence: Longer holidays do not compensate for consistently low wages.
collocations: compensate for; compensate workers; adequately compensate
root_analysis: com-(一起) + pens(秤重、支付, 同 expense/pension) + -ate → 秤平、補足
synonyms: make up for; offset; reimburse; counterbalance
notes: compensate for 的 for 不能省

example_sentence: Analysts attribute the drop in sales to the rise of online shopping.
collocations: attribute the rise to; be attributed to; widely attributed
root_analysis: at-(朝向) + tribut(給予, 同 tribute/contribute/distribute) → 把原因歸給…
notes: attribute A to B 的搭配一定要記

example_sentence: Rapid urbanisation makes some loss of farmland inevitable.
collocations: an inevitable consequence; an inevitable decline; almost inevitable
root_analysis: in-(不) + evit(避開, 同 evade/evitable) + -able → 無法避開的
synonyms: unavoidable; inescapable; certain; bound to happen

example_sentence: Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to coastal communities.
collocations: pose a threat; pose a risk; pose a challenge; pose a question
root_analysis: pos(放置, 同 position/expose/compose) → 把某物放到眼前 → 造成、提出
notes: pose a threat / pose a risk 是閱讀高頻搭配

example_sentence: Readers should be aware of the political bias of the newspapers they follow.
collocations: media bias; political bias; a bias towards; unconscious bias
root_analysis: 原指保齡球球體偏一邊滾的斜度 → 偏向某一邊

example_sentence: The city has invested heavily in transport infrastructure over the past decade.
collocations: invest in infrastructure; ageing infrastructure; transport infrastructure
root_analysis: infra-(在下面, 同 infrared 紅外線) + structure(結構) → 撐在底下的結構
synonyms: public facilities; basic systems; utilities; networks

example_sentence: Schools are gradually integrating digital tools into everyday lessons.
collocations: integrate into; fully integrated; integrate with
root_analysis: integr(完整, 同 integrity/entire) + -ate → 併成完整的一體

example_sentence: Planting trees can partly offset the emissions produced by air travel.
collocations: offset emissions; offset the impact; partly offset
root_analysis: off(離開) + set(放置) → 放到另一邊去抵掉
synonyms: counterbalance; compensate for; cancel out; counteract

example_sentence: Sales dipped briefly in 2012 before recovering the following year.
collocations: dip slightly; a slight dip; dip below
root_analysis: 古英語 dyppan 浸一下 → 短暫沉下去又起來

example_sentence: The graph shows a slump in manufacturing output during the recession.
collocations: a slump in sales; an economic slump; slump to a low
root_analysis: 擬聲字，東西「噗通」塌下去的聲音 → 突然垮掉

example_sentence: Fish stocks dwindled steadily as commercial fishing expanded.
collocations: dwindle steadily; dwindling numbers; dwindle to almost nothing
root_analysis: 古英語 dwinan 枯萎 → 一點一點縮小到幾乎沒有

example_sentence: After a sharp rise, the figure plateaued at around 60 per cent.

root_analysis: 法文 plat(平的, 同 plate/plain) → 高原 → 走成平的一段
synonyms: level off; stabilise; flatten out; remain steady
notes: 名詞、動詞都可用；plateau at + 數值

example_sentence: Energy consumption rose quickly and then levelled off at 90 units.
collocations: level off at; begin to level off; levelling off
root_analysis: level(水平) + off → 從斜的走成水平
synonyms: plateau; stabilise; flatten out; even out

example_sentence: Prices stabilised at just under two dollars per litre after 2016.
collocations: stabilise at; prices stabilised; begin to stabilise
root_analysis: sta(站立, 同 stand/static/stable) + -ise → 站得住不再晃
synonyms: level off; steady; remain constant; settle

example_sentence: Between 2005 and 2010, sales fluctuated between 20 and 35 million units.
collocations: fluctuate wildly; fluctuate between; figures fluctuated
root_analysis: flu(流動, 同 fluid/influence/fluent) + -ate → 像水一樣起起伏伏
synonyms: vary; oscillate; swing; go up and down
notes: 描述不規則變化的首選字；fluctuate between A and B　｜　AWL Sublist 8

example_sentence: The proportion of rural residents remained constant at 15 per cent.
collocations: remain constant; a constant rate; constant throughout
root_analysis: con-(完全) + sta(站立, 同 stand/stable) → 完全站著不動
notes: AWL Sublist 3

example_sentence: Unemployment peaked at 12 per cent in 2009 before falling steadily.
collocations: peak at; reach a peak; peak in 2009
root_analysis: peak 山頂 → 圖上的最高點
synonyms: reach a maximum; culminate; top out; hit a high
notes: peak at + 數值 / peak in + 年份，介系詞不要搞混

example_sentence: The graph reaches a trough of just 5,000 visitors in January.
collocations: reach a trough; a trough of; the trough of the cycle
root_analysis: 古英語 trog 食槽 → 凹下去的地方 → 谷底
synonyms: low point; bottom; minimum; lowest level

example_sentence: Car sales bottomed out in 2013 and then began to recover.
collocations: bottom out at; bottom out in 2013; finally bottom out
root_analysis: bottom(底) + out → 走到底了，不會再往下
synonyms: reach the lowest point; hit rock bottom; stop falling

example_sentence: Tourism rebounded strongly in the two years after the crisis.
collocations: rebound strongly; a sharp rebound; rebound to
root_analysis: re-(回) + bound(彈跳, 同 bounce) → 撞到底再彈回來
synonyms: recover; bounce back; pick up; revive

example_sentence: Demand for housing outstripped supply throughout the decade.
collocations: outstrip supply; outstrip growth; far outstrip
root_analysis: out-(超過) + strip(奔跑, 舊義) → 跑贏對方
synonyms: exceed; surpass; overtake; be greater than

example_sentence: The number of graduates rose steadily from 2000 to 2015.
collocations: rise steadily; steadily increase; grow steadily
root_analysis: stead(位置, 同 instead/homestead) + -y + -ly → 一直待在同一個節奏
synonyms: consistently; gradually; progressively; at a constant rate

example_sentence: Internet use grew dramatically after broadband became affordable.
collocations: rise dramatically; fall dramatically; change dramatically
root_analysis: drama(戲劇, 希臘 dran 行動) + -ic + -ally → 像戲劇一樣誇張

example_sentence: Spending on transport increased only marginally over the period.
collocations: increase marginally; marginally higher; differ marginally
root_analysis: margin(邊緣, 同 margin 頁邊) + -al + -ly → 只在邊緣動一點點

example_sentence: Figures for the two cities differ considerably in the second half of the period.

root_analysis: con-(完全) + sider(星星, 原指觀星占卜 → 仔細考量) + -ably → 值得注意的程度

example_sentence: The chart shows a gradual shift from coal to renewable sources.
collocations: a gradual increase; a gradual decline; a gradual shift
root_analysis: grad(步伐, 同 grade/graduate/progress) + -ual → 一步一步來的

example_sentence: Approximately one in five households owned two or more cars.

root_analysis: ad-(接近) + proxim(最近的, 同 proximity/approach) + -ate + -ly → 靠近某個數
synonyms: roughly; about; around; in the region of

example_sentence: Spending on housing and transport rose to 30 and 18 per cent respectively.

root_analysis: re-(回) + spect(看, 同 inspect/respect/spectator) + -ive + -ly → 各自回頭對應著看

example_sentence: Sales in Europe fell, whereas the figure for Asia more than doubled.

notes: AWL Sublist 5

example_sentence: Online sales overtook high-street sales for the first time in 2019.

root_analysis: over-(越過) + take → 從後面追上去越過

example_sentence: Male graduates outnumbered female graduates by roughly two to one.

example_sentence: Carbon emissions from transport halved between 2010 and 2030.

synonyms: fall by half; be cut in half; drop 50 per cent

example_sentence: Renewable sources accounted for just under a third of total output.
collocations: account for 30 per cent; account for the majority; collectively account for

example_sentence: A large proportion of household waste was sent to landfill.

example_sentence: Overall, the three countries followed very similar trends.

example_sentence: Demand for water remained high throughout the period shown.
collocations: throughout the period; throughout the decade; stable throughout

synonyms: for the whole period; during the entire; across

example_sentence: The final decade witnessed a rapid expansion in solar capacity.

notes: 把時間當主詞：The 1990s witnessed... 讓句型不再都是 X rose

example_sentence: From my perspective, the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks.
collocations: from my perspective; from a student's perspective; from that perspective
root_analysis: per-(透過) + spect(看, 同 inspect/spectator) → 透過我的角度看出去
synonyms: in my view; as I see it; personally; the way I see it
notes: 比 I think 高一級，Part 3 開頭好用

example_sentence: It goes without saying that access to clean water is a basic right.
collocations: it goes without saying that; it almost goes without saying
root_analysis: 「不用講出來就成立」→ 用來引出理所當然的前提
synonyms: obviously; needless to say; it is clear that

example_sentence: To be honest, I had never really thought about that until now.
collocations: to be honest with you; to be perfectly honest
root_analysis: honest(誠實, 拉丁 honos 榮譽) → 把話講白
synonyms: frankly; honestly speaking; to tell the truth

example_sentence: I'd argue that smaller class sizes matter more than new equipment.

synonyms: I would say that; in my opinion; my view is that

root_analysis: de-(向下) + pend(懸掛, 同 pendant/suspend) → 掛在某個條件底下

example_sentence: I have mixed feelings about working from home permanently.
collocations: have mixed feelings about; mixed feelings on the subject
root_analysis: mixed(混合的) + feelings → 心裡兩種感覺混在一起
synonyms: be in two minds about; be torn about; feel ambivalent

example_sentence: I got completely hooked on documentaries during the lockdown.

synonyms: be addicted to; be really into; can't get enough of

example_sentence: My sister has a real knack for picking up new languages.

synonyms: have a talent for; be good at; have a gift for

example_sentence: It took me a few weeks to get the hang of cooking for myself.

root_analysis: hang(懸掛的方式) → 摸清楚東西該怎麼掛 → 抓到訣竅
synonyms: get used to; master; pick up; work out how to

example_sentence: Studying abroad really broadened my horizons in ways I did not expect.

root_analysis: horizon(地平線, 希臘 horizein 劃界) → 把看得到的界線往外推
synonyms: widen your outlook; open your mind; expand your world view

example_sentence: Looking back on my school years, I wish I had joined more clubs.
collocations: look back on my school days; looking back on it now
root_analysis: look + back + on → 回頭去看那段時間
synonyms: reflect on; recall; think back to
notes: Part 2 講過去經驗的收尾句型

example_sentence: One trip in particular stands out because it was my first time abroad.
collocations: stand out from the crowd; really stands out; stand out as
root_analysis: stand + out → 從一排東西裡站出來被看見
synonyms: be memorable; be noticeable; be distinctive

example_sentence: I was completely worn out after two hours of commuting each way.
collocations: be worn out after; completely worn out; feel worn out
root_analysis: wear(磨損) + out → 被磨到光了
synonyms: be exhausted; be drained; be shattered

example_sentence: Cooking is how I unwind after a long day at university.

root_analysis: un-(解開) + wind(纏繞, 同 winding 蜿蜒) → 把纏緊的線鬆開
synonyms: relax; wind down; switch off; de-stress

example_sentence: I tend to procrastinate whenever a deadline feels far away.
collocations: tend to procrastinate; stop procrastinating; procrastinate over
root_analysis: pro-(向前) + cras(明天, 拉丁 cras) + -ate → 一直往明天推
synonyms: put things off; delay; stall; drag your feet

word: off the top of my head
example_sentence: Off the top of my head, I'd say around half of my friends cycle to work.
collocations: off the top of my head; just off the top of my head
root_analysis: 從腦袋最上層直接抓 → 沒細想就講
synonyms: without thinking too hard; at a rough guess; spontaneously
notes: 被問到數據或清單時的救命句，講完就能給個大概答案

word: now that I think about it
example_sentence: Now that I think about it, my hometown has changed enormously.

root_analysis: 把「我正在想」這件事講出來 → 自然地買到幾秒鐘
synonyms: come to think of it; actually; on reflection

root_analysis: tough(硬的、難啃的) → 這題不好答
synonyms: that's a difficult question; I've never thought about that

example_sentence: How can I put this — the service was efficient but not exactly friendly.
collocations: how can I put this; how should I put it
root_analysis: put(放置、表達) → 「我該怎麼把這件事放成話」
synonyms: how shall I say it; let me put it this way

example_sentence: More often than not, I end up studying in a café rather than at home.

root_analysis: 「是的次數多過不是的次數」→ 通常
synonyms: usually; in most cases; generally; as a rule

example_sentence: I still go back to my old neighbourhood every now and then.

root_analysis: 一下 now 一下 then → 不規律地偶爾發生
synonyms: occasionally; from time to time; once in a while

example_sentence: To some extent I agree, though I think cost is the bigger issue.

root_analysis: ex-(向外) + tend(伸展, 同 extend/tension) → 伸展到某個程度
synonyms: partly; up to a point; in some ways

example_sentence: By and large, people in my city are happy with the transport system.

root_analysis: 航海術語：by(順風) 與 large(側風) 兩種情況都算 → 大致上
synonyms: generally; on the whole; for the most part

example_sentence: Public transport is hands down the cheapest way to get around here.
collocations: hands down the best; win hands down
root_analysis: 賽馬領先太多，騎師可以放下韁繩 → 毫無懸念

example_sentence: Long working hours take a heavy toll on people's mental health.

root_analysis: toll 原指過路費 → 走這條路要付出的代價

example_sentence: Online courses can help bridge the gap between rural and urban students.
collocations: bridge the gap between; help bridge the gap; bridge the digital gap
root_analysis: bridge(橋) 當動詞 → 在落差上架一座橋
synonyms: close the gap; narrow the divide; reconcile

example_sentence: Social media is a double-edged sword: it connects people but also spreads rumours.

root_analysis: 把比賽規則改掉的東西 → 徹底改變局面

root_analysis: disguise(偽裝) → 好事偽裝成壞事來
synonyms: a hidden benefit; a silver lining; good news in the end

example_sentence: You have to weigh up the cost against the time you would save.
collocations: weigh up the pros and cons; weigh up the options; weigh up carefully
root_analysis: weigh(秤重) + up → 兩邊放上秤來比

example_sentence: Even small changes at home can make a real difference over time.
collocations: make a real difference; make a big difference; make all the difference
root_analysis: differ(分開, 同 differ/defer) → 造出一個差別來
synonyms: have an impact; count; matter; be significant

example_sentence: Teachers play a key role in whether students enjoy reading at all.
collocations: play a key role in; play a major role; play a part in
root_analysis: role 原指演員台詞捲軸 → 在這件事裡演的角色
synonyms: be central to; be crucial in; contribute significantly

example_sentence: In the end it comes down to whether people can afford the fares.
collocations: it comes down to; ultimately comes down to; come down to money
root_analysis: 一路降下來，最後落在那一件事上
synonyms: boil down to; be a question of; hinge on

example_sentence: The bottom line is that most people simply do not have the time.
collocations: the bottom line is that; the bottom line for me
root_analysis: 財報最底下那一行結論 → 最關鍵的一點
synonyms: the key point; what it really comes down to; the essential point

example_sentence: Cycling to work is cheaper and healthier in the long run.
collocations: in the long run; pay off in the long run; better in the long run
root_analysis: run(一段路程) → 跑很長一段之後來看
synonyms: in the long term; over time; eventually; ultimately

example_sentence: Most families would be better off if childcare were subsidised.
collocations: be better off; financially better off; we'd be better off
root_analysis: off 指「處境」（如 well off 有錢）→ 處在更好的位置
synonyms: be in a better position; benefit more; gain from it
